output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $15,000 to run a school garden and garden-based English language program
output.summary: A contractor will oversee family outreach and on-boarding, garden upkeep and planting, and develop and carry out a garden-based English Language Development (ELD) and health curriculum. The cost may not exceed $15,000 for September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Approves free hosting and support of the ImBlaze platform from Big Picture Company, with student data access
output.summary: The Big Picture Company (doing business as BPL) will host, maintain, upgrade and support the ImBlaze platform for the district at no cost. A separate student data privacy agreement covers the company's access to student data. The agreement runs October 1, 2021 to August 31, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

vendor.name: The Big Picture Company dba BPL

output.headline: Adopts a resolution allowing virtual board and commission meetings in December 2021
output.summary: The board is adopting a resolution that makes the findings needed to hold meetings of district bodies covered by the Brown Act (California's open meetings law) virtually, in specified circumstances. The item has no cost.

output.headline: Sets up no-cost paid internships with Regional Center of the East Bay for students with disabilities
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the Regional Center of the East Bay lets the district and the Regional Center arrange and supervise paid internships for students ages 18-22 who are Regional Center clients and have an Individualized Education Plan (IEP). It costs the district nothing. It runs August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2024. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

vendor.name: Regional Center of the East Bay

output.headline: Approves up to $1,125,011 for Shah Kawasaki Architects to design the Coliseum Prep Academy expansion

money.evidence: in the not to-exceed amount of $1,125,011.00

schools: Coliseum Prep Academy at Havenscourt High School site
output.summary: The board is approving an agreement with Shah Kawasaki Architects for design services for the design-build expansion of the Coliseum Prep Academy at Havenscourt High School site. The cap of $1,125,011 includes up to $100,000 for additional services and up to $23,350 for reimbursable expenses. Work is scheduled from November 18, 2021 to March 31, 2025.

output.headline: Lets Thornhill Elementary and St. John's Episcopal Church enter each other's adjacent property, at no cost
output.summary: Under this right of entry agreement, the district and St. John's Episcopal Church may access each other's adjacent properties, Thornhill Elementary School and the church, at times and as described in the agreement. It costs the district nothing and runs October 12, 2021 through October 12, 2026. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Accepts up to $1,000,000 from the City of Oakland for food and garden programs at the Central Kitchen and farm
output.summary: The City of Oakland will fund environmental, food and garden programming at the district's Central Kitchen, Education Center and Instructional Farm. The grant may not exceed $1,000,000 and covers July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2023. The Community Schools and Student Services Department is handling it. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a coordinator up to $28,234 to run student support teams at Peralta Elementary
output.summary: A contractor will serve as Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) Coordinator at Peralta Elementary School. The role oversees mental health interns, instructional aides, after-school tutoring, referrals and Student Success Teams, and helps the principal plan interventions and track 504 Plans. The cost may not exceed $28,234 for August 9, 2021 through May 25, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Refugee & Immigrant Transitions up to $60,000 for classes, tutoring and language help for refugees
output.summary: Refugee & Immigrant Transitions will teach English classes to up to 90 newly arrived refugee adults, provide home tutoring for at least 20 refugee students, and staff three Community Navigators for families who speak less common languages. It will also run after-school tutoring at Fremont High School and Oakland International High School and interpret for district staff. The cost may not exceed $60,000 for October 18, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a coordinator up to $25,000 to coach 100-150 teachers through teaching credential assessments
output.summary: A contractor will serve as Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA) Coordinator for potentially 100-150 district teachers. The work includes a 10-week course for the EdTPA and CalTPA assessments, individual coaching, office hours and case management so teachers finish and pass on time. The cost may not exceed $25,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Girls Inc. of Alameda County up to $60,000 for reading support at Acorn Woodland Elementary
output.summary: Girls Inc. of Alameda County will act as lead agency to support the lowest-performing readers at Acorn Woodland Elementary School, meeting with students in small groups and one on one for extra reading and homework help. The cost may not exceed $60,000 for September 6, 2021 through May 27, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Adds $200,000 for Fagen Friedman & Fulfrost legal services, bringing the 2021-22 limit to $500,000
output.summary: This amendment adds $200,000 to the district's agreement with the law firm Fagen Friedman & Fulfrost, LLP for legal services on an as-needed basis. The total for the 2021-2022 fiscal year is now capped at $500,000. All other terms of the agreement stay the same.

output.headline: Pays Luna Dance Institute up to $23,200 to train child development center teachers to teach through dance
output.summary: Luna Dance Institute will give the district's child development center teachers workshops and coaching so they can bring dance into their lessons for children ages 3-5. The cost may not exceed $23,200 for August 23, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Consortium up to $27,500 for college and career advising for 65 LIFE Academy seniors
output.summary: East Bay Consortium (EBC) will give extra high school and college advising to 65 seniors at LIFE Academy. The cost may not exceed $27,500 for September 1, 2021 through May 27, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $40,000 for virtual technology-pathway support at Sojourner Truth Independent Study
output.summary: A contractor will give students virtual instructional support centered on a technology career pathway, including monthly work-based learning, internship and job readiness, and e-portfolios, at the Sojourner Truth Independent Study Program. The cost may not exceed $40,000 for August 31, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a clinical supervisor up to $17,600 for mental health trainees at Oakland International High
output.summary: A contractor will act as clinical supervisor for two multilingual associate trainees who provide mental health services to students at Oakland International High School. The cost may not exceed $17,600 for August 30, 2021 through May 27, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $26,950 for a student support specialist at Bunche Academy
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will provide a Student Support Specialist at Ralph J. Bunche Academy who works with teachers on tutoring, study skills, organization and motivation for students in the Hospitality, Tourism and Recreation Pathway. The cost may not exceed $26,950 for September 1, 2021 through May 31, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $91,250 for Be the Change Consulting to support Black student reparations task force work

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $91,250.00

output.summary: The board is approving a contract with Be the Change Consulting to create agendas, facilitate planning sessions and provide overall support for the CORE Team, the Black Student and Families Thriving Task Force and related workgroups. The work is tied to the board's Reparations for Black Students resolution. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $91,250. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $94,999 for Spearitwurx to run community listening sessions for Black Thriving Indicators

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $94,999.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Spearitwurx to design a healing-centered engagement approach for the CORE Team and the Black Student and Families Thriving Task Force. It will also run community listening sessions to help develop Black Thriving Indicators, tied to the Reparations for Black Students resolution. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $94,999. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Approves district participation in the Clean Mobility Options Voucher Pilot Program
output.summary: The board adopts Resolution No. 2122-0037, approving the district's participation in the Clean Mobility Options Voucher Pilot Program. The Risk Management Department is handling the item. The official text does not state a cost or what the program provides.

output.headline: Pays Junk King up to $40,000 to haul away old furniture and equipment from schools
output.summary: Junk King Contra Costa will coordinate removing and disposing of worn-out items such as musical and kitchen equipment, file cabinets, copiers and pallets from school sites and departments. The cost may not exceed $40,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays City Print & Mail up to $90,000 for district printing and mailing
output.summary: City Print & Mail will provide printing and mailing services for the whole district and suggest ways to keep costs down. The cost may not exceed $90,000 for September 7, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays All Smogs Done up to $4,000 to smog-check district vehicles
output.summary: All Smogs Done will perform smog checks on district gasoline, hybrid and diesel vehicles that fall within the age and vehicle-number rules listed in the agreement. The cost may not exceed $4,000 for August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Seven Eleven Body Shop up to $85,000 to maintain and repair district vehicles
output.summary: Seven Eleven Body Shop will maintain the Warehouse Distribution Department's fleet, repair any collision damage, and provide emergency roadside help and other expertise. The cost may not exceed $85,000 for September 7, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Wheelchair Transport up to $95,000 to take students in wheelchairs to and from school
output.summary: Bay Area Wheelchair Transport will drive students who use wheelchairs between home and school and look after them on the trip. The cost may not exceed $95,000 for September 8, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Approves Personnel Report No. 2122-0003 from the Talent/Human Resources Department
output.summary: The board approves a personnel report from the Talent/Human Resources Department. The official text for this item does not list the individual actions or any dollar amounts in the report.

output.headline: Pays Center for Transformative Teacher Training up to $26,800 for coaching web tools at Community United
output.summary: The Center for Transformative Teacher Training will provide web-based tools that Real Time Teacher Coaches use to collect confidential information at Community United Elementary School. The cost may not exceed $26,800, and the agreement period is short, October 15 through October 31, 2021. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Adventure Time up to $32,000 for reading and social-emotional support at Chabot Elementary
output.summary: Adventure Time will provide "between the bells" reading and Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) support for students at risk at Chabot Elementary School. The cost may not exceed $32,000 for August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $7,500 for Across Lines to map options for regional elementary school enrollment

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $7,500.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Across Lines, LLC to analyze and present options for dividing the district into regions for elementary school enrollment. It will use census block group and attendance area data and present the options as maps and data tables for the Student Assignment Department. It runs August 1, 2021 through May 1, 2022 and is capped at $7,500. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $4,000 for a contractor to build an enrollment help site for families in ZenDesk

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $4,000.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with an individual contractor to build a ZenDesk knowledge website for families on the enrollment website, with a staff-only section for Student Welcome Center staff. The work includes gathering content from district offices, launching the site and training staff, and may include some project management. It runs September 13, 2021 through January 15, 2022 and is capped at $4,000. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $95,000 for a project manager to run the ParentSquare communication rollout

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $95,000.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with an individual contractor to manage the district's continued adoption of ParentSquare, a parent communication tool. The work includes supporting school sites and central offices, helping with help desk tickets and working with the IT team. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $95,000. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Mills College up to $34,000 for coaching and training for teachers of long-term English learners
output.summary: Mills College will provide planning, teacher community sessions, individual leadership coaching and teacher stipends for district teachers of Long-Term English Learners. The cost may not exceed $34,000 for October 12, 2021 through May 27, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $227,500 for soccer, tutoring and mentoring for new refugee students
schools: San Antonio Park Middle School Program
output.summary: Soccer Without Borders will serve at least 120 newly arrived refugee and asylum-seeking students in grades 5-12 with bi-weekly soccer training, weekly games, tutoring and mentorship at the San Antonio Park Middle School Program and several school sites. It will also run a week-long summer 2022 soccer camp for at least 150 newly arrived students. The cost may not exceed $227,500 for October 18, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Adds $174,600 in City of Oakland grant funds for student internship stipends; extends term to May 2022
output.summary: This second amendment to a grant agreement with the City of Oakland (through the Oakland Fund for Children and Youth) adds $174,600, raising the agreement's maximum from $380,000 to $554,600. The money pays stipends for students in summer internships in the Linked Learning ECCCO program at 13 high schools. It also extends the term from June 30, 2020 to May 31, 2022, so part of the extended period has already passed.

vendor.name: City of Oakland (Oakland Fund for Children and Youth)

output.headline: Accepts a $50,000 grant from the California School-Age Consortium for early childhood education programs
output.summary: The board is accepting a $50,000 grant earned through the state's Quality Rating and Improvement System for California State Preschool Programs. The money comes from the California School-age Consortium on behalf of the California Department of Education. It will support high-quality early childhood education programs in the district.

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $20,000 to evaluate the district's federal human trafficking prevention grant program
output.summary: A contractor will spend 160 hours designing and running the evaluation of the Federal Human Trafficking Youth Prevention Education (HTYPE) Grant, including pre- and post-tests for students and staff and a review of training results. The cost may not exceed $20,000 for September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Wellness Together up to $50,000 for a mental health consultant at two middle schools
output.summary: Wellness Together will provide a mental health consultant for 30 weeks, giving 357 hours of Tier II (targeted) support at Edna Brewer Middle School and 357 hours at Claremont Middle School. The cost may not exceed $50,000 for September 27, 2021 through May 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $24,000 to mentor the new High School Network Superintendent
output.summary: A consultant will mentor and advise the district's new High School Network Superintendent on priorities, school re-entry plans, secondary education strategy, and building school leaders' use of data, with weekly check-ins. The cost may not exceed $24,000 for September 1, 2021 through May 27, 2022. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Mentoring Medicine & Science up to $10,695 for health career classes at Dewey Academy
output.summary: Mentoring Medicine & Science, Inc. will teach concurrent enrollment classes at Dewey Academy on health careers, including EMT work, sports medicine and medical imaging, plus professional skills for the health industry. The cost may not exceed $10,695 for October 15 through December 17, 2021. The agreement period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,732 for Bay Area Community Resources to staff outdoor time at Markham Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $25,732.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Bay Area Community Resources to provide two staff members who support students in grades TK-5 during outdoor times at Markham Elementary School. The contract runs from August 23, 2021 through May 25, 2022 and is capped at $25,732. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $60,000 for Bay Area Community Resources to support newcomer refugee students from Central America

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Bay Area Community Resources for safety and case management support for refugee and asylee students from Central America, including a classroom-based program and work with community groups to improve safety in district high schools. It runs August 30, 2021 through May 27, 2022 and is capped at $60,000. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $35,000 for HERO Inc. mentoring and social skills programs at Piedmont Avenue Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $35,000.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with HERO, Inc. to provide mentoring services at Piedmont Avenue Elementary School, including social skills lessons, a leadership program, staff training and organized recess. It targets Title I, Latino, African American and second-language students. It runs August 9, 2021 through May 25, 2022 and is capped at $35,000. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $9,625 for Cantare Con Vivo music classes in 10 early grade classrooms at Laurel Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $9,625.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Cantare Con Vivo to teach music in 10 TK-2nd grade classrooms at Laurel Elementary School, with 25 sessions per classroom. The lessons cover music basics and support language development and teamwork. It runs August 9, 2021 through May 27, 2022 and is capped at $9,625. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $79,920 for Teaching Strategies to train preschool teachers and staff

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $79,920.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Teaching Strategies, LLC to provide professional development for teachers and staff in the district's Early Childhood Development Department. Topics include getting started with its preschool approach, planning to meet the needs of children and families, and in-depth investigations. It runs October 11, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is capped at $79,920. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $22,500 for Attitudinal Healing Connection artist to teach arts lessons at Hoover Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $22,500.00

output.summary: The board is confirming a contract with Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc. to provide one resident artist who works alongside teachers during in-person math or English class time at Hoover Elementary School. The artist leads arts-integrated lessons for K-2 classes in six-week cycles. It runs August 23, 2021 through May 26, 2022 and is capped at $22,500. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Awards $189,400 to Rook Electric for a year of security camera repair and maintenance at various sites
output.summary: The board is approving an agreement with Rook Electric, the lowest responsive bidder, to repair and maintain security cameras at various district sites. The work includes troubleshooting, repairs, remote help, onsite maintenance and cleaning. The $189,400 includes a $23,000 reimbursable fee. It is scheduled to run about 365 days, from November 18, 2021 to November 18, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies the Board President's appointment of a member to the Measure N College and Career Readiness Commission
output.summary: The board is confirming the Board President's appointment of Katharina Nunez-Adler to the Measure N - College and Career Readiness Commission. The first term runs from November 18, 2021 to January 31, 2022, followed by a reappointment from February 1, 2022 to January 31, 2024. The item has no cost.
